title: Columbia band, Zulu parade with Armstrong, subbing for Bunk, Lindsay's band
summary: One long answer: joining the Columbia band at fourteen, his first street parade with Louis Armstrong, subbing for Bunk, hearing Oliver, and joining Joe Lindsay's band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Joe Johnson. Joe Johnson. Joe Johnson and Bunk and Buddy Beteete they all played by the same little style. So that kept me going. And so about 1915 I was close to 14 years old. I started playing with the whole Columbia band, the whole Columbia band, a cornet player called Tick Chambers. The band was getting ready to come north and so George Foster was in the band, Pop Foster, and they told him, says the kid uptown in Losing Avenue, play like Bunk, Lee Collins, why don't you give Lee Collins a chance and let him play cornet in this band. So I joined the Columbia band very young, very young. I used to wear Mark Loenis' long pants and coat and to go play in this band and go to school in the daytime, playing the band all night long and go to school in the daytime. Tom LaFont School was not so far from my home where I lived, on Losing Avenue. So about 1915, 16, the Zulu parade, the drummer by the name of Black Benny hired me to play a street parade. And this parade was Louis Armstrong. I had seen Louis Armstrong play before, but I hadn't seen him. The first time I'd seen him play, he was with the Joneses band, they come to play for the dedication of the playground at Tom LaFont, him and Kid Renee at that time. But I had never seen him in a band professional. So Benny hired me for this parade, because the musician was hard to get. I was very young to play for the Zulus. And the band was Louis Armstrong, another corner player by the name of Schatz, and myself. We three played. So that was a great thrill of my life, because I had never played a street parade before. That's a good plan. I had never played a street parade before. It was for a real-age battle house club, the Zulus. So I noticed Louis had a similar touch of bunk too. He was playing on the other bunk, so that just set me right, because it brought my style right to me. So at that time I thought I was really going good. So bunk, bunk was, bunk was playing down the spot jobs around, I think the Eagle band had broken up or something. Tubby Hall and left and went to come to Chicago, he was drumming with him at that time. Bache was playing in the honky tonks, forgot to call tooddle him and grabbing Franklin. So bunk didn't show up on the job once. He was on his little drinking spree. So they come and got me to play in the great bunk's place. So that really made me feel good, not because bunk was drunk, didn't show up, because I had a chance to sub for bunk. I was thinking that I was getting some plays, time to go in, time I was good enough to go in bunk's place, because bunk was the number one corner at that time. Joe Oliver at that time was a butler on Magazine Street. He was playing and coming out and listening to that room. So I had heard, I didn't hear Joe Oliver play until he come to work for Pete Lallers, Pete Lallers Cabaret. Pete Lallers and I was, it was Joe Oliver and Lorenzo Teal, they had a bunch playing together. So I used to go, I was too young to go into the halls, I'd stand outside and listen to Joe. Joe was a little different from the bunk. My man was very powerful, listen to him. So I kept on going, kept on going, kept on going until I, Louis Armstrong, little band, East Comin' the Duckies, little band, was managed by a great friend of mine called little Joe Lindsay. Joe Lindsay is a brown skin jazz band. So I joined Joe Lindsay's band where Louis was playing and Louis was, went in the honky-tonks back at that time and I was playing with little Joe Lindsay's band. So, by that time I got a chance to go, to go work for, go work down in the district, what they call Storyville now. Buddy Petit was working with Jimmy Noon in a place called Few Clothes Place. You heard of that place?
